issues.description: In the solution Lecture class the private fields are declared using snake_case identifiers (lecture_name, number_of_inscribed_students, number_of_guest_students, number_of_lecturers, number_of_tutors) but the constructor and all methods use camelCase identifiers (lectureName, numberOfInscribedStudents, numberOfGuestStudents, numberOfLecturers, numberOfTutors). Example: solution/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Lecture.java declares private String lecture_name; (lines 6-6) while the constructor assigns this.lectureName = lectureName; (line 14). The problem statement's UML uses the camelCase names (lectureName, numberOfInscribedStudents, numberOfGuestStudents, numberOfLecturers, numberOfTutors). This naming mismatch causes compilation errors (unresolved symbol: lectureName) and will confuse or block students who rely on the solution as reference.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the identifier names consistent. Recommended: rename the private fields in solution/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Lecture.java to the camelCase names used in the constructor and UML (lectureName, numberOfInscribedStudents, numberOfGuestStudents, numberOfLecturers, numberOfTutors). Alternatively, change all constructor parameters and method references to match the declared snake_case fields, but prefer renaming the fields to camelCase to follow Java conventions and match the problem statement and existing method code.
